_doc: Revert-verify mutants for ticket efe993e1 (req 78c46697-6d6f-4ad3-8c98-f8f3b3507231, PR fix/shapeloader-quoted-label). Run from the repo root: python3 -I ~/.claude/bin/mutant-driver.py <this file> after setting `tree` and `subject` to YOUR checkout (both absolute). The diff is ONE line — registerCandidate now strips the surrounding quotes from exo__Asset_label with the predicate copied verbatim from indexUidLabel — so the guards are enumerated INSIDE that line per integration-test-revert-verify §A8: the two literal character classes (the leading and the trailing anchored ['"] ), and the `g` flag. Each carries a mutant; M1 removes the predicate outright. M1/M3/M4/M5 share a RED set (they all leave a quote attached, so labelToIRI fails and the def is dropped) — the overlap is legitimate: they are DIFFERENT guards of the same expression and each must redden, not each must redden something unique. M2 is the adressed one: dropping the apostrophe from the class leaves the double-quoted axis green and reddens only the single-quoted one. ⛔ ONE conceivable mutation carries no mutant deliberately: replacing the anchored predicate with an unanchored `.replace(/["']/g, "")` (strip EVERY quote, not just the surrounding pair) is behaviourally equivalent on any admissible input — a label with an INTERIOR quote fails Namespace.fromPropertyKey under every state of this code, so no observable differs and an axis for it would be vacuous. Expectations were derived axis-by-axis (what does each one assert), not from the mutant's theme — §A44. ⛔ REVIEW ROUND 1 (ORCH): B3 originally carried BOTH the bare and the quoted def and asserted the quoted one was defined, so it reddened whenever B1 did — i.e. it reddened for the absence of its NEIGHBOUR, not for its own declared subject, and a control that reddens with its target is not a control (§A37; the expectation must follow from the axis's OWN subject, §A44). It was split: B3 is now the pure control — the bare def alone, asserted against LITERAL expected values with no reference to the quoted side — and stays GREEN under every mutant, which is the stronger claim (the unquoted path is intact even with the fix removed); B3b keeps the quoted-vs-bare comparison and legitimately reddens with B1/B2 because it covers the quoted side too. B6 (FS/graph parity) reddens with them for the same honest reason: a dropped FS shape breaks parity. B3, B4 (basename fallback) and B5 (a human label stays unadmitted) are the three axes GREEN under every mutant.
